dedupe_keys.name: route choice estimation in rail transit systems using smart card data handling vehicle schedule and walking time uncertainties

description: The implemented Python method estimates passenger routes using only fare-gate entry/exit observations. It infers train arrivals from exit-volume peaks and aligns feasible vehicle locations with passenger timing while accounting for walking and schedule uncertainty. The Lisbon application finds that many passengers favour fewer transfers, with some favouring shorter distances. It does not require an exact train timetable or direct passenger-tracking sensors, but its inferred routes remain model estimates. The project catalogue and current public repository identify the same software; no standard software licence is detected. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with open document or data access and licence label cc-by-4.0. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened. It models network flow through inferred passenger journeys.
